seoTitle: Vitals Shopify App Tutorial for Beginners
metaDescription: A full walkthrough of the Vitals Shopify app covering installation, setup, pricing, and how it replaces dozens of separate conversion apps.
intro: The Vitals app bundles dozens of conversion and marketing tools into a single Shopify app, which can save you from installing and paying for separate plugins one by one. Instead of managing ten different apps for reviews, bundles, and upsells, everything lives inside one dashboard reachable straight from your Shopify admin. This guide walks a beginner through what that dashboard actually looks like, how to turn on individual tools like Product Reviews, and where to go once you want to fine-tune how a feature displays on your store.

steps.heading: Find Vitals in your Shopify admin
steps.body: Once installed, Vitals appears as its own entry under Apps in the left-hand Shopify admin menu, alongside your usual Home, Orders, Products, and Marketing links. Opening it drops you straight into the "More tools for your store" section, which is organized into labeled groups — Trust, Upsells, UX, Conversion, and more — each showing three featured tools with a "View more" link to see the rest of that category.

image.caption: The Vitals dashboard inside the Shopify admin, showing tools grouped by category: Trust, Upsells, and UX.

steps.heading: Scroll through the full tool catalog
steps.body: Scrolling down reveals more categories, including Conversion tools like Back in Stock, Wishlist, and Animated Add to Cart, plus a Frequently Bought Together module that's already generating a sample bundle recommendation based on your store's products. This is the core of what makes Vitals useful for a beginner: instead of researching and installing a separate app for each of these features, you're scanning one long, organized list and switching on only what your store actually needs.

image.caption: More tool categories further down the dashboard, including a live Frequently Bought Together bundle example.

steps.heading: Open a tool and activate it
steps.body: Clicking into a specific tool, like Product Reviews, brings up a dedicated screen describing what it does — in this case, collecting, importing, and displaying reviews with photos to boost trust and conversions. Underneath the description is a checklist of what's included: displaying reviews in a grid or list on product pages, automating review requests by email, importing reviews from other apps or CSV files, and featuring select reviews on your homepage. Nothing is live yet at this point; you still need to press Activate App to turn it on for your store.

image.caption: The Product Reviews tool page, with its feature checklist and the Activate App button before it's turned on.

steps.heading: Configure the tool's settings
steps.body: Once a tool is active, it gets its own set of tabs — Dashboard, Reviews, Moderation, Featured, Import, Request Reviews, Groups, Settings, and Analytics for Product Reviews specifically. Inside Settings, a left-hand list breaks widgets down further, like Reviews Widget, Star Ratings, Reviews Carousel, and Happy Customers Page, each with its own configuration panel. For Star Ratings, you can toggle whether stars display under the product name, set the star size in pixels, choose left, center, or right alignment separately for desktop and mobile, and even edit the exact display format using variables like {{ stars }} and {{ averageRating }}.

image.caption: The Star Ratings settings panel for Product Reviews, with alignment, size, and format controls for the product page.

steps.heading: Turn on only what your store needs
steps.body: With dozens of tools available, the temptation is to activate everything at once, but that defeats the purpose of using an all-in-one app in the first place. Start with two or three tools that map directly to a problem you already have — reviews if you lack social proof, Back in Stock if you're losing sales on out-of-stock items, or a bundle tool if your average order value is lower than you'd like. Each active tool adds a small amount of page weight, so activating everything indiscriminately can slow your storefront down even though it's all coming from one app instead of many.

steps.heading: Check pricing before you rely on it long-term
steps.body: Vitals is typically available with a free trial period, which is enough time to activate a handful of tools and see whether they move the needle on your actual sales data before you commit to a paid plan. Compare the cost of your intended Vitals plan against what you'd otherwise spend on separate apps for reviews, upsells, and pop-ups individually — for many stores running four or more of these features, Vitals works out cheaper even before counting the time saved managing one dashboard instead of several.

faq.question: Is Vitals free to try on Shopify?
faq.answer: Vitals offers a free trial period so you can test its features, like Product Reviews or Back in Stock, before committing to a paid plan.

faq.question: Does Vitals replace multiple separate Shopify apps?
faq.answer: Yes, that's its main selling point — bundling tools like reviews, bundles, upsells, and pop-ups into one dashboard instead of installing dozens of separate apps.

faq.question: Is Vitals good for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, each tool inside Vitals has its own description, checklist of features, and a simple Activate App button, so you can turn features on one at a time without needing prior setup experience.

faq.question: How much does Vitals cost after the trial?
faq.answer: Pricing depends on the plan tier you choose, so check the app's current pricing page directly for the latest rates before the trial ends.

faq.question: Will activating a lot of Vitals tools slow down my store?
faq.answer: It can — each active tool adds some page weight, so it's worth only activating the tools that solve a real problem for your store rather than switching everything on at once.
